claim: With the confocal laser's 488 nm line at 100% level through the 4x objective, 7.0 mW reached the sample plane, measured with a power meter on this instrument on 2026-09-09.

numbers.name: illumination_power
numbers.note: read at the sample plane with the head's wavelength set to this line

validity_conditions:
This instrument, the confocal laser's 488 nm line, 4x objective, level 100%, with the worksheet's reference state: mirror in, multiband out, IR in. Worksheet Power row 52. Measured 2026-09-09 by Kyu Hwan Choi and Saksham Malik with a Thorlabs PM100A and an S120C or S121C photodiode head (which of the two is not known), the wavelength set to each line; the person confirmed on 2026-09-24 that every spot was inside the sensor, so this is the power at the sample and not a lower bound. Valid ten years from 2026-09-24 as the person stated.

The level is in `validity` as illumination_level 1 (100% written as a fraction), because it is the one condition of this measurement that is a quantity: a caller asking at another level gets a miss named, not this number. `illumination_level` is not yet a registered quantity.

WHAT '100%' IS: the level setting in the acquisition software the measurement was taken with. This system cannot yet command a level -- the combiner's per-line power word is deliberately not transmitted (lunf_per_line_power_is_not_transmittable) -- so this is the output at full level, not a map from a command this system sends to an output.

THE LEVEL SWEEP, at 20x only, is partial and is not entered as linearity: rows 46-51: 0% 0, 5% blank, 10% blank, 30% 1.3, 50% 3, 100% 6.9 mW. Nothing here says the output scales with the level.

NOT MEASURED: 405 nm, and 100x for any line. Nothing here extrapolates to either -- transmission does not carry across objectives, and an oil objective needs oil between lens and meter.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: a change to the laser, its fibre or the light path between them and the sample; a re-measurement supersedes it.
